unmappable_fields.reason: No business-tier or subscription-level concept exists anywhere in django/contrib/auth/. AbstractBaseUser (base_user.py:43-164) and AbstractUser (models.py:446-514) define only authentication and identity fields; choices-based tier classification is purely application-domain logic.
unmappable_fields.migration_strategy: Keep as a custom field on the AbstractBaseUser subclass: `profile_tier = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=[('free','Free'),('pro','Pro'),('enterprise','Enterprise')], default='free')`. Generate a migration adding this column. No auth integration point is needed — access is purely via the model instance.
unmappable_fields.evidence: django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:43 (AbstractBaseUser class definition, no tier field); django/contrib/auth/models.py:446 (AbstractUser class definition, no tier field)

unmappable_fields.reason: Django contrib.auth has no SSO or external identity provider field. AbstractBaseUser provides only password (base_user.py:44) and last_login (base_user.py:45) as DB fields. AbstractUser adds username (models.py:456) and email (models.py:470) but neither is intended as an opaque external identifier. The unique=True + nullable pattern for SSO IDs has no auth equivalent.
unmappable_fields.migration_strategy: Keep as a custom field: `external_sso_id = models.CharField(max_length=255, unique=True, null=True, blank=True)`. Add a DB index for SSO lookup performance. Implement a custom authentication backend (subclassing ModelBackend) that looks up users by external_sso_id when the SSO provider authenticates; wire it into AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS in settings.
unmappable_fields.evidence: django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:44-45 (only password+last_login in AbstractBaseUser); django/contrib/auth/models.py:456-470 (username/email in AbstractUser, neither suitable for opaque SSO IDs)

unmappable_fields.reason: The closest temporal field in contrib.auth is last_login (base_user.py:45), updated by the update_last_login receiver (models.py:18-24) on the user_logged_in signal (signals.py:3). However last_login tracks authentication events, not external system synchronisation. There is no sync-timestamp concept in django/contrib/auth/.
unmappable_fields.migration_strategy: Keep as a custom field: `last_sync_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)`. Update it in the SSO sync code path (e.g. a Celery task or post-save signal in the application). Do NOT repurpose last_login — doing so would break the update_last_login wiring in AuthConfig.ready() (apps.py:27-32) and the session auth hash mechanism in AbstractBaseUser.get_session_auth_hash() (base_user.py:132-149).
unmappable_fields.evidence: django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:45 (last_login DateTimeField — auth-event semantics only); django/contrib/auth/models.py:18-24 (update_last_login sets last_login = timezone.now() on login, not on sync); django/contrib/auth/apps.py:27-32 (update_last_login wired to user_logged_in, not a sync signal)
